rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): suppress native browser context menu
rawCommits.body:
Right-clicking empty AURA chrome was showing the WebView2 / Chromium
native menu (Back, Refresh, Save as, Print, More tools, Inspect),
breaking the desktop OS feel. Install a single document-level listener
that defers to any in-app onContextMenu (DesktopContextMenu,
NotesEntryContextMenu, ProcessCanvas, ...) via event.defaultPrevented,
and otherwise cancels the native menu. Inside editable text fields
(input, textarea, contenteditable) we replace the native menu with a
compact in-app Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All so right-click editing
still works without giving up control of the chrome.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: suppress native browser context menu

rawCommits.subject: fix(desktop): widen top-edge resize hit area on Windows
rawCommits.body:
The borderless main window inherits tao's default WM_NCHITTEST
behavior, which only reports HTTOP within SM_CYFRAME (~4 logical
px) of the top edge. Combined with the floating titlebar pill
that begins 5 px below the window edge, hitting the resize zone
required pixel-perfect aim.

Install a Win32 subclass on the main HWND that returns
HTTOP/HTTOPLEFT/HTTOPRIGHT for any cursor inside a 10-logical-px
band along the top, falling through to DefSubclassProc for every
other position so titlebar drag, side resize, and Chromium
app-region all keep working unchanged. The subclass is dispatched
before tao's by virtue of being installed last, becomes a no-op
while the window is maximized, and re-reads DPI on each hit-test
so it stays consistent across mixed-DPI monitor setups.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: widen top-edge resize hit area on Windows

rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): defer-open pattern for async-loading modals
rawCommits.body:
When the user clicked Delete on an agent attached to multiple
projects, the confirm modal opened immediately, then janked: the
"Delete" button widened to "Delete and remove from N projects" and
a cascade-warning paragraph appeared once bindings finished loading.
Same flicker existed for the marketplace Hire modal (in-modal
spinner -> project list) and the Tier subscription modal ("Loading
plan details..." -> tier grid).

Introduce useDeferredModalOpen, a tiny shared hook that runs the
caller's prepare() (e.g. cascade.refresh / projectsStore.refresh /
billingStore.fetchSubscription), keeps the modal closed and shows a
disabled trigger button until the prepare resolves, and only then
flips isOpen true. A 3000ms failsafe opens the modal even if prepare
never settles. Stale resolutions from a previous open cycle are
ignored via an internal cycle token.

Apply to three call sites:
- DeleteAgentConfirmModal (AgentList + AgentInfoPanel) - also shorten
  the cascade label from "Delete and remove from N projects" to
  "Delete (N projects)" so width is stable across binding counts.
- HireProjectPickerModal (MarketplaceMainPanel) - drop the in-modal
  spinner; the per-card Hire button disables briefly while preparing.
- TierSubscriptionModal (OrgSettingsPanel via OrgSettingsRewards /
  OrgSettingsBilling) - read subscription from billing-store instead
  of fetching on open; the Upgrade / Change Plan trigger disables
  briefly while preparing.

The remaining modals from the audit (AgentSelectorModal,
BuyCreditsModal, ProjectSettingsModal, etc.) are deliberately left
for follow-up PRs - the shared hook is the substrate for those.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: defer-open pattern for async-loading modals

rawCommits.subject: feat: split AURA into dev and stable build channels
rawCommits.body:
Introduce a build-time channel selector on aura-os-core
(`stable-channel` default, `dev-channel` opt-in via cargo features)
so a `cargo run`-built dev AURA can run side-by-side with the
installed stable AURA on one machine without colliding on data
dirs, ports, single-instance locks, skills trees, or window
identity. Remote services stay shared via .env.

The new `Channel` enum in `aura-os-core::channel` is the single
source of truth for every per-channel identifier: data dir name
(`aura` vs `aura-dev`), skills home (`~/.aura` vs `~/.aura-dev`),
Windows single-instance mutex, window/menu title, embedded
desktop server port (19847 vs 19848), standalone server port
(3100 vs 3101), harness sidecar port (19080 vs 19081), default
harness URL port (8080 vs 8081), and updater enablement (off in
dev so a cargo-built shell can never silently replace itself
with the stable installer).

`cargo run -p aura-os-desktop` and the `scripts/dev/*` runners
default to the dev channel via cargo's default feature. The
release pipeline (`cargo packager`, `verify-desktop.mjs`, the
`release-stable` and `release-nightly` workflows) builds with
`--no-default-features --features stable-channel`. The desktop
crate disables default features on its `aura-os-core` and
`aura-os-server` deps so a stable packaging build cannot
accidentally pull in `dev-channel` from a transitive default.

Dev script defaults bumped to dev-channel ports (Vite 5174,
mobile backend 3101) so a developer running `npm run dev` or the
mobile runner does not bind on top of an installed stable AURA.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: split AURA into dev and stable build channels

rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): re-enable 3D chat mode with image-first flow
rawCommits.body:
Bring back the 3D pill in the chat mode selector and rewire it so
the only valid path is "generate an image first, then convert it to
3D" -- exactly how the standalone AURA 3D app works. Manual image
attachments for chat 3D mode are disabled because the proxy decode-
and-forward route is broken; the legacy code path is left in place
but commented out so flipping it back on is trivial once the proxy
is fixed.

The input bar now derives its 3D source from the most recent
successful generate_image tool result in the thread, surfaces it
as a "Source for 3D" thumbnail above the textarea, blocks Send with
a "switch to Image mode" hint until one exists, and dispatches the
3D request via generate3dStream's URL form. The resolved-send
pipeline carries sourceImageUrl through to both the live and
queue-replay paths.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: re-enable 3D chat mode with image-first flow

rawCommits.subject: fix(aura3d): stop appending style-lock suffix to image prompts
rawCommits.body:
The AURA 3D app's Image tab was the only call site appending the
product-photography STYLE_LOCK_SUFFIX to user prompts. Send the prompt
verbatim instead so image generation behaves consistently with chat
/image and /3d. The constant is retained so `stripStyleLock` can still
clean the suffix off legacy artifacts persisted before this change.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: stop appending style-lock suffix to image prompts

rawCommits.subject: fix(agents): recognize renamed CEO via system-prompt prefix
rawCommits.body:
After renaming the bootstrap CEO (e.g. "CEO" -> "Maia") and re-logging
in, the server was creating a duplicate "CEO" agent. `looks_like_ceo`
only recognised renamed CEOs via the locally-stamped
`bootstrap:ceo_agent_id` setting or an exact name+role both equal to
"CEO". CEOs created before commit 2dabef61a (the stamping fix) never
had the local stamp, so a post-rename login fell through both checks
and `dedupe_ceo_agents` returned no canonical, causing
`setup_ceo_agent` to mint a fresh duplicate.

Add a third identity signal: the canonical CEO `system_prompt` prefix
("You are the CEO SuperAgent"), extracted into a shared constant so
the matcher and the template stay in lock-step. The agent editor
preserves `system_prompt` on save unless the user explicitly rewrites
it, so this prefix survives a rename and lets the dedupe step pick the
older renamed CEO as canonical and best-effort delete the freshly-
minted duplicate on the next setup call.

Adds four unit tests: renamed-name-only, full rename, arbitrary system
prompt is not a CEO, and a drift guard that `ceo_system_prompt()`
always starts with `CEO_SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX`.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: recognize renamed CEO via system-prompt prefix

rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): copy menu for selected non-editable text
rawCommits.body:
After turning off the native browser context menu, right-clicking a
text selection in chat / LLM output (which renders as static markdown,
not a contenteditable) just suppressed the menu and showed nothing.
Detect a non-collapsed window.getSelection() that covers the click
target and surface a Copy-only menu in that case. Editable fields,
app-claimed events, and plain non-editable empty areas keep their
existing behavior unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: copy menu for selected non-editable text

rawCommits.subject: Rework chat 3D mode as in-bar two-step image-then-3D pipeline
rawCommits.body:
- Adds STYLE_LOCK_SUFFIX to the chat 3D image step only; image mode and

- Replaces the "Generate an image first" gate with a removable pinned
  source thumb owned by chat-ui-store; one-shot seeding from thread

- Splits the 3D wire variant into image_step / model_step branches in

- Relocates STYLE_LOCK_SUFFIX to interface/src/constants/generation.ts.

rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): drop unsupported cargo build flags from cargo packager call
rawCommits.body:
cargo-packager 0.11.8's CLI does not accept --no-default-features or
--features; those are cargo-build flags. The stable-channel feature is
already wired in via `before-packaging-command` in
apps/aura-os-desktop/Cargo.toml, so the packager applies it correctly
during the build step it runs internally. Passing the flags to
`cargo packager` itself was failing CI with `unexpected argument`.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: drop unsupported cargo build flags from cargo packager call

rawCommits.cleanSubject: remove style lock from image generation prompts

rawCommits.subject: fix(interface): show titlebar Update pill at full accent saturation
rawCommits.body:
The PillButton wraps zui's Button with variant="filled", but zui dims any
non-selected, non-noDim button to 60% opacity. That washed out both the
accent background and the pill's hard-coded dark text, making the Update
pill look muted and the label look gray. Opt out via dimUnselected={false}
so the pill renders at the full --color-accent at rest and hover darkens
to --color-accent-hover via zui's existing .filled:hover rule.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: show titlebar Update pill at full accent saturation

rawCommits.subject: fix(interface): fall back to "New Agent" label when agent name is missing
rawCommits.body:
Sidebar rows in AgentList, the project explorer, and the Tasks project
tree rendered an empty label whenever an agent's name was blank or
absent, leaving avatar-only rows with no identifier. Add a shared
agentDisplayName helper that yields "New Agent" for null/undefined or
whitespace-only names, and route the sidebar surfaces (label, avatar
name, archive aria-label, delete-confirm modal, row data attribute)
through it so we always render a recognizable placeholder.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: fall back to "New Agent" label when agent name is missing

rawCommits.subject: fix(interface): suppress focus-visible outline on dialog/modal wrappers
rawCommits.body:
Container elements with `tabindex="-1"`, `role="dialog"`, or
`aria-modal="true"` are focused programmatically for keyboard /
screen-reader scope management, not as tab stops. When the user pressed
Shift (or Shift+Tab) Chromium flipped into keyboard-modality, and the
zui Modal's `modalRef.current?.focus()` call on its `tabIndex={-1}`
wrapper triggered the global `:focus-visible` rule and painted a 2px
white ring around the entire modal box. Extend the existing
`#root` / `.titlebar-drag` opt-out to also cover those container
patterns (and both `:focus` and `:focus-visible` for keyboard-modality
edge cases) so high-level wrappers never paint a focus ring while real
interactive controls keep their accessible focus indicator.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: suppress focus-visible outline on dialog/modal wrappers

rawCommits.subject: feat(theme): jet-black modal background with per-mode override
rawCommits.body:
Introduces a new ZUI-level `--color-modal-bg` token (jet black `#000`
in dark mode, `var(--color-elevated)` in light mode) that the Modal
component now reads instead of the generic elevated surface, so all
modals inherit the new look without affecting dropdowns, cards, or
other elevated chrome.

Surfaces the token in Settings > Appearance > Custom colors as a
paired Dark + Light editor backed by an extended
`useThemeOverrides.setToken(token, value, targetTheme?)` API and the
new `darkOverrides` / `lightOverrides` exports, letting users tune
both modes' modal background simultaneously regardless of the
currently active theme.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: jet-black modal background with per-mode override

Swap the rest/hover opacity values on the base Button so unselected,

Refresh the dimUnselected JSDoc and PillButton's opt-out rationale to

rendered.title: Native chrome polish, dual build channels, and a rebuilt 3D chat flow
rendered.intro: A dense nightly that reshaped how AURA feels as a desktop app: the browser context menu is gone in favor of a native-feeling in-app one, Windows users can finally grab the top edge to resize, and modals stop flickering as their data loads. Underneath, AURA now ships as separate dev and stable channels so contributors can run a `cargo` build alongside the installed app, and the chat 3D mode came back as a proper two-step image-then-model pipeline.

entries.title: Native browser context menu replaced with an in-app menu
entries.summary: Right-clicking AURA chrome no longer surfaces the WebView2/Chromium menu; editable fields get a compact Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All instead.

items.text: A document-level listener now suppresses the native Back/Refresh/Inspect menu across AURA chrome while still deferring to in-app handlers like DesktopContextMenu, NotesEntryContextMenu, and ProcessCanvas via defaultPrevented.
Inputs, textareas, and contenteditable fields get a purpose-built in-app Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All menu so right-click editing keeps working without ceding the chrome to the browser.

entries.title: Windows top-edge resize is no longer pixel-perfect
entries.summary: A Win32 WM_NCHITTEST subclass widens the borderless main window's top resize band to 10 logical pixels.

items.text: On Windows, the top of the main window now reports HTTOP/HTTOPLEFT/HTTOPRIGHT across a 10 px band instead of tao's default ~4 px frame, so grabbing the edge to resize stops fighting the floating titlebar pill.

The subclass installs after tao's so it runs first, becomes a no-op while maximized, and re-reads DPI on each hit-test to stay correct on mixed-DPI multi-monitor setups; titlebar drag, side resize, and Chromium app-region behavior are unchanged.

entries.title: Async-loading modals open once at their final size
entries.summary: A new useDeferredModalOpen hook fixes the jank where Delete, Hire, and Tier modals popped open and then resized as data arrived.

items.text: Introduced a shared useDeferredModalOpen hook that runs a prepare() step (cascade refresh, project list fetch, billing subscription) with the trigger disabled, then opens the modal at its final state — with a 3000 ms failsafe and a cycle token that drops stale resolutions.

Wired the pattern into DeleteAgentConfirmModal (AgentList + AgentInfoPanel), the marketplace HireProjectPickerModal, and the TierSubscriptionModal, and shortened the cascade label to "Delete (N projects)" so the footer width stays stable across binding counts.

entries.title: AURA splits into dev and stable build channels
entries.summary: A build-time channel selector lets a `cargo run` dev build coexist with the installed stable AURA without colliding on data dirs, ports, or single-instance locks.

items.text: Added a Channel enum in aura-os-core that drives every per-channel identifier — data dir (`aura` vs `aura-dev`), skills home, Windows single-instance mutex, window/menu title, and the embedded server, standalone server, harness sidecar, and harness URL ports.

The updater is disabled in dev builds so a `cargo run` shell can never silently replace itself with the stable installer, and the desktop crate disables default features on its core/server deps so a packaging build can't pull in dev-channel transitively.

Release pipelines (desktop-validate, release-nightly, release-stable) and verify-desktop.mjs now build with `--no-default-features --features stable-channel`, while `cargo run` and the scripts/dev runners default to dev — Vite moves to 5174 and the mobile backend to 3101 so `npm run dev` doesn't bind on top of an installed AURA.

entries.title: 3D chat mode returns with an image-first pipeline
entries.summary: The 3D pill is back in the chat mode selector, wired to require an existing generated image as the source — and the standalone AURA 3D Image tab now sends prompts verbatim.

items.text: Re-enabled 3D mode in chat: the input bar derives its source from the most recent successful generate_image tool result, surfaces it as a "Source for 3D" thumbnail, blocks Send with a switch-to-Image hint until a source exists, and dispatches via generate3dStream's URL form on both live and queue-replay paths.

The AURA 3D app's Image tab no longer appends the product-photography STYLE_LOCK_SUFFIX, so its prompts behave consistently with /image and /3d; the constant is retained only so stripStyleLock can clean up legacy artifacts.

entries.title: Two-step 3D pipeline, theme tokens, and chat empty-state polish
entries.summary: A long evening of interface work: chat 3D became a true in-bar two-step flow, modals went jet-black with per-mode overrides, the right-click menu learned to copy selected text, and a packager CI break was fixed.

items.text: Reworked chat 3D as an in-bar image_step → model_step pipeline: replaced the "generate an image first" gate with a removable pinned source thumb owned by chat-ui-store, split the wire variant in resolve-send and the chat-stream hooks, and later dropped the style-lock suffix from the image step entirely.

The native-menu override now shows a Copy-only menu when right-clicking inside a non-collapsed selection on static markdown or LLM output, so selecting and copying chat replies works again after the native menu was suppressed.

Modals adopt a new ZUI `--color-modal-bg` token (jet black in dark mode, elevated surface in light) without affecting dropdowns or cards, and Settings → Appearance → Custom colors gained a paired Dark + Light editor backed by an extended setToken(token, value, targetTheme?) API.

Inverted ZUI Button dimming so unselected buttons sit at full opacity at rest and fade on hover, and explicitly opted the titlebar Update PillButton out of dimming so it renders at full accent saturation.

Redesigned the empty-chat state: four prompt-suggestion chips now float between the input bar and taskbar as a 2x2 grid with Lucide icons and proper gaps, and the empty-state input bar pulse slowed from 2s to 6s so it breathes instead of blinking.

Sidebars now fall back to a "New Agent" label via a shared agentDisplayName helper for blank or whitespace-only names, the bottom-bar environment slot reserves space while agent metadata loads so siblings don't shift, the desktop right-click label was shortened to "Background", and dialog/modal wrappers no longer paint a stray focus ring on Shift-keypress.

Project Settings can now attach an Orbit repo via the same create-default / create-custom / link-existing choices as the new-project flow, with the server's update_project handler calling orbit.ensure_repo when a fresh owner+repo is supplied.
Server-side, a renamed bootstrap CEO is now recognized via a shared CEO_SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX so post-rename logins stop minting duplicate "CEO" agents when the local stamp is missing.

Unblocked CI by removing `--no-default-features --features stable-channel` from the `cargo packager` invocations in desktop-validate, release-nightly, and release-stable — packager 0.11.8 rejects those as cargo-build flags, and the channel feature is already applied via the crate's before-packaging-command.
Small AURA 3D fix-up: removed a stray "what" from the image prompt placeholder.

highlights: Native browser context menu replaced with in-app Cut/Copy/Paste
Windows top-edge resize hit area widened to 10 px
Dev and stable channels can now run side-by-side
3D chat mode rebuilt as in-bar image-then-3D pipeline
Async modals open once at final size instead of janking
Jet-black modal background with per-mode color override
